elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "each Party's aggregate liability to the other Parties arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed ..." — symmetric, applies to every Party including us and the counterparties.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap is a single limb — "the Capital Costs and O&M Costs paid or payable by that Party ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim". There is no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 21.3: "Under no circumstances shall any Party be liable to any other Party ... for any indirect or consequential loss or damage" — mutual and left untouched.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out: "Except for a Party's ... breach of Paragraph 31 (Confidentiality) ... in respect of which no limit shall apply".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list is limited to indemnification, Paragraph 31 confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears anywhere in the rendered text.
Carve-out opens "Except for a Party's indemnification obligations ... in respect of which no limit shall apply", which reaches the 21.2 third-party indemnity.
"its gross negligence" is inside the "no limit shall apply" carve-out.
"or its wilful misconduct, in respect of which no limit shall apply".
Fraud is absent from the carve-out list in the inserted sentence.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the inserted sentence or elsewhere in Paragraph 21.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No language stating that our payment obligations (e.g. Capital Costs / O&M Costs contributions) are not "damages" subject to the cap; the cap sentence is silent on payment obligations.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's aggregate liability to the other Parties ... shall not exceed" — one cap applying equally to all Parties; no residual unlimited-Customer language remains.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Cap equals "the Capital Costs and O&M Costs paid or payable by that Party under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" — a 12-month measure of the Agreement's whole payment stream (this consortium agreement has no item called "Fees"), so it is not an illusory sub-set.
"Except for a Party's indemnification obligations ... in respect of which no limit shall apply".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "its breach of Paragraph 31 (Confidentiality)" sits outside the cap.
"its gross negligence" listed in the carve-out.
"its wilful misconduct" listed in the carve-out.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the single inserted sentence delivers a mutual aggregate cap measured on twelve months of the Agreement's actual payment stream, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct expressly outside the cap.

Preferred is not complete: no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud or infringement of the other Party's IP; the Customer-payment-obligations exclusion is also absent. If the preferred level is wanted, add the floor and extend the exception list, and state that amounts payable by us under the Agreement are not "damages" subject to the cap.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion at the end of Paragraph 21, no deletion or paraphrase of 21.1–21.3, the favourable mutual exclusion in 21.3 is retained, and no extras (no survival tail, procedure or additional damages categories) were added.

Drafting risk to tighten without expanding scope: "in respect of which no limit shall apply" read at large could be argued to override the retained Customer-favourable Schedule B share limitation in 21.2 ("no indemnifying Party shall be obligated to contribute more than its share of liability as per Schedule B"). Repair by narrowing to "in respect of which the limit in this Subparagraph shall not apply" so the exception operates only on the new cap.

Verify two references in the operative text before sending: (i) that Paragraph 31 is in fact the Confidentiality paragraph, otherwise the confidentiality carve-out is a dangling cross-reference; and (ii) that "Capital Costs" and "O&M Costs" are defined terms capturing the full payment stream, since no definitions were resolved in the record — if either fails, the cap basis or the confidentiality carve-out becomes unenforceable as drafted.
